name: Ornitholestes
currentFacts: Its name means 'bird robber'.
It was a small, fast, and agile predator.
Contrary to early restorations, it likely did not have a horn on its nose.

name: Compsognathus
currentFacts: It was a very small, bipedal carnivore.
Its fossils were found with the remains of small lizards in their stomachs.
It lived on an archipelago in a shallow tropical sea.

name: Guanlong
currentFacts: It is one of the earliest known tyrannosauroids.
It possessed a large, fragile crest on its head.
Its name means 'crowned dragon'.

name: Proceratosaurus
currentFacts: It possessed a small crest on its snout.
It is one of the oldest known members of the tyrannosaur lineage.
Only a partial skull has been found.

name: Metriacanthosaurus
currentFacts: Its name means 'moderately-spined lizard'.
It had tall neural spines on its back, though not forming a full sail.
It was a medium-sized apex predator of its ecosystem.

name: Eustreptospondylus
currentFacts: It lived in an island environment.
It may have scavenged marine carcasses that washed ashore.
The single known specimen is considered a subadult.

name: Piatnitzkysaurus
currentFacts: It was a medium-sized bipedal predator.
It represents one of the few known Middle Jurassic theropods from South America.
It shares primitive traits with basal tetanurans.

name: Marshosaurus
currentFacts: It was a medium-sized predator in the Morrison Formation.
It was rarer than competitors like Allosaurus.
Its exact taxonomic position within tetanurans is debated.

name: Stokesosaurus
currentFacts: It is an early member of the tyrannosauroid family.
It was a small, agile predator.
Similar fossils found in England were later reclassified as a separate genus, Juratyrant.

name: Tanycolagreus
currentFacts: Its name means 'long-limbed hunter'.
It was slightly larger and more robust than its relative Ornitholestes.
It had a long, low skull compared to other small theropods.

name: Sciurumimus
currentFacts: The fossil preserves filamentous feathers, especially along the tail.
Its name means 'squirrel mimic' due to its bushy tail.
Initially thought to be a megalosauroid, it may be a primitive coelurosaur.

name: Juravenator
currentFacts: Its fossil shows patches of scaly skin, suggesting a lack of feathers in some areas.
It had unusually large eyes, suited for nocturnal hunting.
It was a very small, agile predator.

name: Diplodocus
currentFacts: It had an exceptionally long, whip-like tail.
Its center of gravity allowed it to rear up on its hind legs.
Its teeth were peg-like and restricted to the front of the jaw.

name: Apatosaurus
currentFacts: It had a very robust, heavily built skeleton compared to Diplodocus.
Its tail may have been able to crack like a whip, producing a loud sound.
It was an abundant herbivore in the Morrison Formation.

name: Brontosaurus
currentFacts: Its name means 'thunder lizard'.
It had a slightly thinner and less robust neck than Apatosaurus.
It is one of the most culturally famous dinosaur names.

name: Camarasaurus
currentFacts: It had a boxy, blunt skull with large, spoon-shaped teeth.
Its name means 'chambered lizard', referring to hollow chambers in its vertebrae.
It likely fed on tough, fibrous vegetation.

name: Giraffatitan
currentFacts: It is one of the tallest known dinosaurs.
A famous, nearly complete skeleton is mounted in the natural history museum in Berlin.
It was adapted for high-browsing on conifer trees.

name: Barosaurus
currentFacts: It is closely related to Diplodocus but had a significantly longer neck.
Its neck vertebrae were exceptionally elongated.
A famous mount at the AMNH shows it rearing up to defend against an Allosaurus.

name: Dicraeosaurus
currentFacts: It had tall, bifurcated (Y-shaped) neural spines on its neck and back.
It had a relatively short neck for a sauropod.
It was a low-browser in an ecosystem dominated by taller sauropods.

name: Omeisaurus
currentFacts: It had a long, heavily built neck.
Some species assigned to it may have had a tail club.
It was a common large herbivore in its ecosystem.

name: Vulcanodon
currentFacts: It is one of the earliest known true sauropods.
Its forelimbs retained some primitive traits while its hindlimbs were column-like.
It lived in a volcanic landscape.

name: Patagosaurus
currentFacts: It was a basal eusauropod with a relatively short neck.
Adults and juveniles were found together, indicating herd living.
It was a dominant herbivore in its South American ecosystem.

name: Cetiosaurus
currentFacts: Its vertebrae lacked the complex hollow air sacs seen in later sauropods.
It was a primitive sauropod weighing roughly 15 tons.
It serves as an important baseline for understanding early sauropod evolution.

name: Spinophorosaurus
currentFacts: It originally was thought to have a spiked tail club (thagomizer), but the spikes were later re-identified as collarbones.
It is one of the best-preserved early sauropods.
Its anatomy provides a crucial link between basal sauropodomorphs and eusauropods.

name: Haplocanthosaurus
currentFacts: It is considered a primitive macronarian sauropod.
It lacked the extreme specialized features of Diplodocus or Camarasaurus.
It was one of the smaller sauropods of the Morrison Formation.

name: Supersaurus
currentFacts: It is among the longest dinosaurs ever discovered.
It was a diplodocid, closely related to Apatosaurus.
Its neck vertebrae were exceptionally elongated and robust.

name: Suuwassea
currentFacts: It is a primitive member of the dicraeosaurid family.
It possessed an extra opening (foramen) in its skull of unknown function.
It provides evidence for early diplodocoid radiation in North America.

name: Jobaria
currentFacts: It had a relatively short, primitive neck compared to later sauropods.
Its spoon-shaped teeth were adapted for nipping branches.
It was the most common large herbivore in its African environment.

name: Bellusaurus
currentFacts: The mass grave suggests a herd perished together in a flash flood.
All known specimens are juveniles.
It was a small macronarian sauropod.

name: Dryosaurus
currentFacts: It was a fast, agile bipedal runner.
It lacked the thumb spikes seen in later iguanodonts.
It was a highly successful, small herbivore of the Morrison Formation.

name: Camptosaurus
currentFacts: It was a heavily built ornithopod that could walk on two or four legs.
It possessed a small, hooved thumb on its hands.
Its beak was toothless, but it had tightly packed cheek teeth.

name: Kentrosaurus
currentFacts: Its back was covered in pairs of plates that transitioned into long spikes near the tail.
It featured a prominent spike pointing backward from each shoulder.
It was smaller and more primitively built than Stegosaurus.

name: Scutellosaurus
currentFacts: It is one of the earliest known armored dinosaurs.
It was a small, lightly built, bipedal herbivore.
Its body was covered in parallel rows of small bony scutes.

name: Scelidosaurus
currentFacts: It was covered in rows of keeled bony armor.
It is considered an early relative of both ankylosaurs and stegosaurs.
It was a quadrupedal browser with a small head and leaf-shaped teeth.

name: Gargoyleosaurus
currentFacts: It is one of the earliest and most complete known ankylosaurs.
Its heavily armored skull had prominent horns on the rear corners.
It had a complex network of nasal passages.

name: Othnielosaurus
currentFacts: It was a small, swift, bipedal herbivore.
It possessed enameled teeth well-adapted to chewing tough vegetation.
Its name honors paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh.

name: Lesothosaurus
currentFacts: One of the earliest known ornithischian dinosaurs.
It had a small, slender body built for fast running.
Its teeth were leaf-shaped, adapted for slicing plant material.

name: Hexinlusaurus
currentFacts: A small, basal neornithischian dinosaur.
It had prominent ridges on its teeth for grinding.
Coexisted with larger dinosaurs like Shunosaurus.

name: Chialingosaurus
currentFacts: It was a very slender and primitive stegosaur.
Named after the Jialing River in Sichuan.
Its plates were narrower and more spine-like compared to later stegosaurs.

name: Tuojiangosaurus
currentFacts: Featured 15 pairs of pointed plates along its back.
Had a distinctive pair of spikes on its shoulders.
Bore a thagomizer with four large spikes at the end of its tail.

name: Dacentrurus
currentFacts: Possessed paired spikes rather than plates along most of its back and tail.
Its front limbs were relatively long for a stegosaur.
The pelvis was exceptionally broad to accommodate a large gut.

name: Miragaia
currentFacts: Had an unusually long neck with at least 17 vertebrae.
Its neck length rivaled some sauropods.
Its back was adorned with paired triangular plates.

name: Hesperosaurus
currentFacts: Closely related to Stegosaurus but had broader, oval-shaped plates.
Its skull was proportionately wider than that of Stegosaurus.
Lived slightly earlier than most Stegosaurus species.

name: Fruitadens
currentFacts: One of the smallest known ornithischian dinosaurs.
Had canine-like tusks in its lower jaw.
Likely an omnivore, eating both plants and small animals or insects.

name: Nanosaurus
currentFacts: A small, agile, bipedal dinosaur.
Othnielosaurus is often considered a synonym of Nanosaurus.
Used speed to escape from contemporary predators like Allosaurus.

name: Rhamphorhynchus
currentFacts: Had a long, stiff tail ending in a diamond-shaped vane.
Its jaws were filled with sharp, forward-pointing teeth for catching fish.
Lacked a bony crest on its head.

name: Dimorphodon
currentFacts: Had a remarkably large, deep skull resembling that of a puffin.
Possessed two distinct types of teeth in its jaws.
Its wings were relatively short, suggesting it was not an oceanic soarer.

name: Pterodactylus
currentFacts: Had a long, pointed beak filled with small teeth.
It was a short-tailed pterosaur (pterodactyloid).
Likely fed on small fish and invertebrates.

name: Anurognathus
currentFacts: Had a very short skull and broad, frog-like mouth.
Unlike its relatives, it had a very short tail.
Likely an aerial insectivore, similar to modern nightjars.

name: Scaphognathus
currentFacts: Had a broader, more robust skull than its relative Rhamphorhynchus.
Its teeth were vertically oriented rather than pointing forward.
Its brain was relatively large compared to other early pterosaurs.

name: Sordes
currentFacts: Provided the first undeniable proof that pterosaurs were covered in fluff.
Had a thick coat of pycnofibers over its body and part of its wings.
Was a small, long-tailed pterosaur.

name: Darwinopterus
currentFacts: A crucial missing link showing modular evolution in pterosaurs.
Had a long tail like early pterosaurs, but the skull of advanced ones.
Exhibited clear sexual dimorphism, with males having head crests.

name: Wukongopterus
currentFacts: Part of the transitional group connecting basal and advanced pterosaurs.
Had a robust tail and elongated cervical vertebrae.
Likely arboreal, navigating through dense forest environments.

name: Kunpengopterus
currentFacts: Recently discovered to possess an opposable thumb.
The opposable thumb suggests it lived and climbed in trees.
It lacked a bony crest on its head.

name: Ctenochasma
currentFacts: Had hundreds of long, thin teeth forming a comb-like structure.
Used its unique jaws to filter-feed on small aquatic organisms.
Was a fully flying equivalent to modern flamingos.

name: Gnathosaurus
currentFacts: Its jaws broadened at the tip into a spoon-like shape.
Possessed over 130 needle-like teeth.
Fed by sweeping its jaws through mud to catch small invertebrates.

name: Cycnorhamphus
currentFacts: Had unusual jaws with a distinctive upward curve or kink.
Likely used its specialized jaws to crush hard-shelled prey.
Lacked teeth in the front portion of its mouth.

name: Germanodactylus
currentFacts: Had a prominent bony crest running along the top of its skull.
Its jaws were mostly toothless at the very front.
Likely hunted fish, similar to modern terns.

name: Pterorhynchus
currentFacts: Preserved an intricate, sail-like crest made of keratin.
Had long hair-like pycnofibers with distinct tufts.
Its tail vane was reinforced by elongated scales.

name: Harpactognathus
currentFacts: One of the few large pterosaurs known from the Morrison Formation.
Had a significant bony crest extending to the tip of its snout.
Its wingspan is estimated to have been around 2.5 meters.

name: Mesadactylus
currentFacts: One of the earliest recognized pterodactyloid pterosaurs in North America.
Was quite small, with an estimated wingspan under 1 meter.
Its isolated bones were initially confused with bird remains.

name: Jianchangnathus
currentFacts: Had a highly robust lower jaw with a prominent chin.
Only three teeth were present in each maxilla.
Its tail was relatively straight and rigid.

name: Fenghuangopterus
currentFacts: A member of the scaphognathine group of pterosaurs.
Had a blunt, short skull packed with vertically oriented teeth.
Provides key insights into early pterosaur diversity in Asia.

name: Liopleurodon
currentFacts: A formidable apex predator of the Jurassic seas.
Though famously portrayed as 25 meters long, it actually reached about 6-7 meters.
Had an exceptionally powerful bite force.

name: Plesiosaurus
currentFacts: Characterized by a small head, long neck, and four large flippers.
Moved through the water by flying with its flippers, like modern sea turtles.
Its diet consisted mainly of fish and small cephalopods.

name: Ichthyosaurus
currentFacts: Convergent evolution gave it a body shape strikingly similar to a modern dolphin.
Gave birth to live young at sea, as proven by fossilized mothers with embryos.
Had massive eyes reinforced by bony rings for deep-water vision.

name: Ophthalmosaurus
currentFacts: Had the largest eyes relative to body size of any known vertebrate.
Its enormous eyes suggest it hunted in deep, dark waters.
Possessed a teardrop-shaped body built for high-speed swimming.

name: Cryptoclidus
currentFacts: Had a surprisingly fragile skull for a marine predator.
Its jaws were lined with dozens of interlocking, needle-like teeth.
Likely fed by trapping small fish and soft-bodied squid.

name: Rhomaleosaurus
currentFacts: A large, robust pliosaur with a powerful build.
Had an internal nasal passage that allowed it to smell underwater.
Hunted other large marine reptiles as well as big fish.

name: Macroplata
currentFacts: Had an unusually long neck for an early pliosaur.
Its skull was robust and crocodilian in shape.
Reached about 4.5 meters in length.

name: Peloneustes
currentFacts: A relatively small pliosaur, measuring around 3 meters long.
Had fewer, more robust teeth than its relatives.
Specialized in hunting hard-shelled prey like ammonites and belemnites.

name: Pliosaurus
currentFacts: An enormous apex predator of the Late Jurassic.
Its skull could reach over 2 meters in length.
Its bite force was powerful enough to crush a car.

name: Simolestes
currentFacts: Had a remarkably short, blunt snout.
Its jaw muscles were exceptionally large, giving it a very powerful bite.
Likely specialized in twisting chunks of flesh off large prey.

name: Temnodontosaurus
currentFacts: One of the largest known ichthyosaurs, reaching up to 12 meters.
An apex predator that fed on other marine reptiles and large cephalopods.
Possessed large, robust teeth with distinct cutting edges.

name: Excalibosaurus
currentFacts: Like Eurhinosaurus, it had an extremely elongated upper jaw.
Its front flippers were much shorter than those of its relatives.
Helps document the evolutionary transition of swordfish-like ichthyosaurs.

name: Morganucodon
currentFacts: One of the earliest and most transitional forms between cynodonts and true mammals.
Had a double jaw joint, a hallmark of early mammalian evolution.
Was a tiny, shrew-like animal that hunted insects at night.

name: Castorocauda
currentFacts: The earliest known mammal-like animal with a beaver-like tail and webbed feet.
Provides evidence that early mammaliaforms were highly specialized, not just generalized shrews.
Preserves the oldest known evidence of mammalian hair.

name: Volaticotherium
currentFacts: The earliest known gliding mammal-like animal.
Pushed back the origin of mammalian gliding flight by 70 million years.
Had sharp teeth adapted for a purely insectivorous diet.

name: Fruitafossor
currentFacts: Had remarkably strong forelimbs adapted for digging, like a modern mole or aardvark.
Its tube-like, rootless teeth were perfectly suited for eating colonial insects like termites.
Shows that early mammals were highly ecologically diverse.

name: Juramaia
currentFacts: The earliest known eutherian (placental) mammal.
Pushed back the divergence date of placental and marsupial mammals by 35 million years.
Its forelimbs indicate it was an agile tree climber.

name: Agilodocodon
currentFacts: An early mammaliaform that was highly adapted for living in trees.
Its teeth suggest it had a specialized diet of tree sap.
Possessed highly flexible wrists and elbows for grasping branches.
